sections.h2: Where to pay and ask questions
sections.html:
Lowndes County runs its property tax out of Valdosta, with the commissioner and the assessors answering different questions. Bills, payments and liens go through the commissioner. Values and special assessment programs go through the assessors.

  • Lowndes County Tax Commissioner: 300 N. Patterson Street, P.O. Box 1409, Valdosta, GA 31601. Phone 229-671-2579, fax 229-671-2599. Counter service runs 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM on weekdays. Drivers have a separate lane that opens half an hour later and closes at 5:00 PM.
  • Lowndes County tax assessors: phone (229) 671-2540.
  • Deed room run by the Superior Court clerk, Lowndes County Judicial Complex, 327 N. Ashley Street, ground-level 1st Floor: copies of your warranty deed.

A payment box for drivers stands on the right side of the Government Building's front lot. If you mail a check, write the bill number on it and include a return envelope if you want a receipt.

sections.h2: Lowndes County housing at a glance
sections.html: Lowndes sits in south Georgia, with Valdosta as its center and roughly 497 square miles of land. The mid-2025 population estimate is 122,867, up 3.9% from 118,259 in 2020. There are 54,425 housing units, and owners occupy 56.9% of homes. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $215,600, so a large share of the county rents, which matters if you are selling a rental or a house with a tenant. Builders pulled 804 permits in 2025.

Tax on land, buildings and business equipment is generally due by November 15 each year. The commissioner mails each bill two months or more before that date, and bills usually reach mailboxes in early October.

Lowndes County property tax calendar and late charges
EventRule
Property returnsFiled from New Year's Day through April 1
Homestead applicationMust reach the office by April 1 to count that year
Appeal of assessmentForty-five days after the notice date
Due date, real estateGenerally November 15, with weekends and holidays pushing it to the next day the office is open
Interest after due dateBank prime rate plus 3%, added monthly
Penalty5% of the tax once 120 days pass, added again every 120 days until 20% is reached
Penalty exceptionA homesteaded parcel whose bill is below $500.00
Lien (FiFa)Recorded by the court if the bill stays unpaid

A mailed check avoids interest only if the postmark falls on or before the due date. Owners can pay in two installments, though interest and penalty attach to whatever remains open after the due date. The office warns that the date may change, so use the one on your bill.

sections.h2: How values are set and challenged
sections.html:
The taxable slice in Georgia is 40% of market value, known as assessed value, and the Lowndes assessors reset it each year. From New Year's Day through April 1, an owner may file a return declaring a proposed value. Should the Board of Assessors see it differently, a notice with the board's own number goes out, usually in May.

Contesting the figure gives you 45 days counted from the notice date. The first hearing belongs to an equalization board or an arbitrator. Still unhappy afterward? Written notice to the assessors moves the case to Superior Court.

  • Value disputes start with the assessors at (229) 671-2540.
  • Billing disputes start with the commissioner at 229-671-2579.
  • One mill raises a dollar on every thousand dollars of assessed value. The county and the school board each vote a rate every year.

Exemptions come off the assessed figure and the millage rate multiplies the remainder. Your current bill shows the Lowndes rate in force.

The cycle opens when a sale closes and its deed is recorded in Valdosta. The assessors then give the parcel a value and mail a notice the following May. When the appeal period closes, they compile the tax digest, an official listing of every owner, street address, legal address, property location, exemption, assessment and tax due. State revenue officials approve that digest before the commissioner prints bills.

Personal property follows a separate track. Boats and motors, tractors, farm equipment and machinery count, and so do furniture, fixtures, equipment, inventory and supplies for a business. Ownership is settled as of New Year's Day, appraisers mail their values every year, and owners get the same 45 day appeal window.

The commissioner hears about a transfer through the recorded deed. If your closing statement prorated the tax, hand that statement to the commissioner yourself.

Four ways work: the counter, the mail, the drive-up box and a credit card. The card company, not the county, adds a convenience fee: 2.57% on Discover, Mastercard and Visa, and 3% on American Express, each with a minimum of $1.50.

Past-due notices are mailed at set intervals, not monthly, so check the balance before you send money. Interest accrues monthly until the balance clears, and a lien can stay on a credit record for at least seven years.

If taxes stay unpaid beyond 90 days after the due date, the Delinquent Tax Office may begin tax sale proceedings. Ask the commissioner before that point about the exact balance and your options.

sections.h2: Who owes the bill when you sell
sections.html:
Whoever held title when the year began gets the bill. A lien is recorded in that person's name unless the commissioner has a contract or closing statement in hand, no more than 90 days after the due date, showing the new owner took on the tax. If tax was prorated at closing, take the signed statement to the Patterson Street office.

State revenue rules put the whole year on the January 1 owner, and a sale the next day earns no refund. Once the deed transfer reaches the office, the buyer may be billed as well.

  1. Get the payoff figure from the commissioner.
  2. Have the closing attorney settle it at the table.
  3. Forward any later bill to the new owner.

A house inherited from a relative or occupied by tenants follows the same path. A cash sale skips the lender's payoff wait, but the tax still has to be settled at closing.

A home qualifies for homestead and business inventory qualifies for freeport. Who owns and lives in the property on January 1 settles eligibility, and the assessors take the filing.

  • Applications are taken year-round, though one arriving after April 1 applies to the following year.
  • Approval carries forward each year at the same address, and a move requires a fresh filing.
  • At age 65, an owner can apply for an additional homestead exemption. Ask the commissioner for the form.
  • Special assessment programs, such as farm and conservation use, are explained by the assessors.

A mobile or modular home counts as personal property, so its owner files a return each year if it sits in the county.

faqs.q: What is the usual Lowndes County due date?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 each year for land, buildings and business equipment. The commissioner cautions that it can change, so check your bill.

faqs.q: What does a late Lowndes County payment add?
faqs.a: Interest runs at the bank prime rate plus 3% each month, and a 5% penalty begins at the 120-day mark, recurring on that cycle until it totals 20%. A homesteaded parcel whose bill is below $500.00 escapes the penalty.

faqs.q: Does the Lowndes County commissioner take cards?
faqs.a: Yes. The card company adds its own fee, 2.57% for Discover, Mastercard and Visa and 3% for American Express, with a $1.50 minimum on each. A drive-up box is also available.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if I sell my Lowndes County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The person who owned the home on January 1 is liable for the whole year, and there is no refund for a later sale. Settle any split in the closing statement and bring a copy to the commissioner.

faqs.q: How long does a Lowndes County owner have to contest a value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. An equalization board or arbitrator hears the case first, and written notice to the assessors keeps it alive for Superior Court.
